question.text: A rod OA hangs from a hinge fixed at point O on a vertical wall. Its lower end, point A, is tied by a weightless string to a fixed point B on a support to the right, at the same height as A. Draw a diagram of the rod alone showing every force acting on it.
conditions: rod is hinged to a wall at O
B is fixed to a support at the same height as A

figure.description: On the left is a vertical wall. Point O is a hinge fixed on this wall, near the top. A rigid rod runs from O down and to the right to its other end, point A. From A, a horizontal massless string runs further right to point B, which is fixed to a second vertical support at the same height as A. The rod slopes downward from the upper-left hinge O to the lower-right end A, and the string AB is horizontal.

solution.approach: The rod is a rigid body in equilibrium under three forces: its own weight, the string tension, and the hinge reaction.

steps.text: Mark the weight of the rod, Mg, acting vertically downward at its centre of mass, the midpoint of OA.
steps.equation: Mg ↓ at the midpoint of OA

steps.text: Mark the string tension T at end A, directed along AB, pulling from A toward B, horizontally away from the wall.
Mark the hinge reaction at O. A hinge can push or pull in any direction, so it has two unknown components at O.
steps.why_this_step: A hinge is not a string, so its reaction is not restricted to one direction.

steps.text: The free body diagram of the rod carries three forces in total.
steps.equation: Mg at the midpoint, T at A along AB, and (Hₒ, Vₒ) at O

final_answer.value: Three forces act on the rod: weight Mg downward at its midpoint, string tension T at A along AB, and a hinge reaction at O with two unknown components Hₒ (horizontal) and Vₒ (vertical).

common_mistakes.text: Drawing the hinge reaction only along the rod's own length, as if it were a string; a hinge can push in any direction, not only along OA.
Leaving out the weight of the rod, treating it as massless like the string; the rod has mass and its weight acts at its midpoint.
